newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow at steady $64-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow at steady $64-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets on Friday were slow, with light sales early at $64.00 per cwt, steady with the majority of cattle sold this week, feedlot sources said.

About 200 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area after a weekly movement of 93,400. No sales were reported Friday in Kansas, the sources said. Weekly sales in Kansas were 98,300 head, according to USDA statistics.
Fed cattle prices this week at $64.00 were up $1.00 from last week, underpinned by a strong beef market, they said.
Beef prices were powered by tight stocks and demand from retailers for supplies to fill coolers the next two weeks for Independence Day holiday promotions, market sources said.
Fed cattle prices next week were seen off $1.00 at $63.00 amid outlooks for slower beef demand, several sources said.

Prices also could be pressured by light demand from packers who will be buying a smaller number of cattle because there will be one less slaughter day due to the holiday in the following week, the sources said.
Declines were seen limited by sales this week which kept feedlots very current in Kansas and the Panhandle.

Sales in Nebraska this week were so brisk that owners pulled unfinished cattle from next week's showlists to meet demand, which will result in lighter numbers of market-ready cattle next week, they said.
